title: Mangled Extremity Severity Score (MESS)
sources: Johansen K, et al. Objective criteria accurately predict amputation following lower extremity trauma. J Trauma. 1990;30(5):568-572
Bosse MJ, et al. A prospective evaluation of the lower-extremity injury-severity scores (LEAP study). J Bone Joint Surg Am. 2001;83(1):3-14
Kauvar DS, et al. Utility of the Mangled Extremity Severity Score in predicting amputation in military lower extremity arterial injury. Ann Vasc Surg. 2018

changelog.change: Initial entry — the 4-component MESS; interactive companion to the mangled-extremity section of the penetrating-regional-trauma reference.

purpose: Scores a severely injured lower (or upper) extremity across four axes to inform the salvage-versus-amputation discussion. Its predictive value is stronger for identifying salvageable limbs (a low score) than for mandating amputation (a high score) — treat it as one input, not a decision.

options.label: Low energy — stab, simple closed fracture, small-calibre GSW
Medium energy — open or multiple fractures, dislocation
High energy — shotgun (close range), high-velocity GSW, crush
Very high energy — the above plus gross contamination, soft-tissue avulsion

items.label: Limb ischemia (double the points if ischemia time > 6 hours — options below already reflect this)

options.label: Reduced pulse but normal perfusion — ≤ 6 h
Reduced pulse but normal perfusion — > 6 h
Pulseless, paraesthesias, diminished capillary refill — ≤ 6 h
Pulseless, paraesthesias, diminished capillary refill — > 6 h

interpretation.label: MESS < 7 — historically associated with a salvageable limb. Low scores are the more reliable end of the score; proceed with limb-salvage assessment (vascular, orthopaedic, plastics) and revascularization if indicated

MESS ≥ 7 — the commonly cited amputation-associated threshold, but multiple validation studies (including LEAP and combat-casualty data) show only modest sensitivity and specificity here. Do NOT use as an automatic indication for amputation — weigh mechanism, ischemia time, associated injuries, contamination, patient factors, and reconstructive resources with the surgical team

notes: Original derivation was retrospective in lower-extremity trauma (Johansen 1990). The prospective LEAP study found MESS (and the other limb-injury scores) did not reliably predict which limbs were ultimately amputated or which salvaged limbs did well functionally — a low score predicting salvage held up better than a high score predicting amputation. Blast, crush, and ballistic mechanisms, polytrauma, and massive-transfusion requirement independently raise amputation rates regardless of the MESS. Warm ischemia beyond ~6 h markedly worsens salvage odds — the ischemia component is doubled for that reason (already built into the options here). Not validated in children.
buildNote: Tier 2 — score components/thresholds are settled but their predictive limits are well documented; framed here as decision support, not a rule. Interactive companion to the mangled-extremity section of `penetrating-regional-trauma`. Ischemia > 6 h doubling is baked into the option list rather than a separate multiplier (additive engine).
